project.description: RFC 0066 Episode 3, layer 4 — the site base: the contracts a served site is made of, and nothing that dresses one. A Navigable is a destination whose whole public contract is "given the query it was reached with, possibly none, the page"; a Router takes a path in and hands a Navigable out; a Site is a router with a name; a SiteHost serves one. How a navigable comes by its HTML — a JS app behind the server's scaffold, a template, a string — is the navigable's own business and not the contract's. The nested demo modules are the proof: each a site of a few pages on the base alone.
